title: 第4回上場企業で金塊マネー循環か　銀行口座の履歴に残る不自然な出入金

translated_text: This is about a company that purchased a large quantity of gold bars from Unbanked (Unbank), a company listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Standard market, but failed to pay over 1.3 billion yen to Unbanked. Tracing the records since gold trading began last summer, hundreds of millions of yen have been transferred to Unbanked multiple times. These amounts roughly match the purchase prices for the gold bars. So where did the funds for the purchase prices come from? The sources of the large deposits that were repeatedly made during the same period as the transactions included familiar company names. In July last year, Unbanked started gold trading at the suggestion of representatives sent from Akatsuki Capital Works (Akatsuki), which had become a major shareholder. They were introduced to two gold suppliers and one buyer, and conducted resale transactions 27 times, but the last two transactions led to payment disputes. As reported, the core of the problem lies not in the gold trading itself, but in the fact that the listed company entered into economically irrational transactions and failed to adequately verify its trading partners, funding sources, and actual controllers.
